title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Chrome and Windows Zero-Days in BlueMoon Attacks
content_md: A rapidly adopted exploit kit, dubbed BlueMoon, chains Chrome and Microsoft Windows zero-days to compromise targets in espionage-focused phishing campaigns. Most observed activity has been linked to China-aligned clusters, although researchers cautioned that the toolkit cannot yet be attributed exclusively to Chinese state-backed operators. The campaign was first observed on August 28, 2026, when TA412, also tracked as JungleBamboo, Violet Typhoon, APT31, and TIDE CASTLE, used BlueMoon against US non-governmental organizations, mining companies, and commodity-trading firms. China-Linked Hackers Exploit Chrome and Windows Zero-Days Within days, the same underlying exploit chain appeared in operations attributed to suspected China-aligned clusters targeting US aerospace companies, Vietnamese manufacturers, and government, financial, and consulting organizations in Indonesia and Singapore. BlueMoon exploits CVE-2026-85046, a type-confusion vulnerability in Chrome’s V8 JavaScript engine , alongside a V8 sandbox escape and CVE-2026-85880, a Windows kernel local privilege-escalation flaw. Attack Flow (Source: ProofPoint) The browser component abuses an optimization error involving Array.prototype.sort and fill() to obtain memory read-and-write primitives in V8’s heap cage. Attackers then manipulate WebAssembly metadata to execute native shellcode beyond the renderer sandbox.
